solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Follow westbound taxi finally stuck in traffic (8)

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left
what comes finally in a word is its closing letter, so only that one is used

blocks.note: to tail someone is to follow them

annotation.surface: A driver trailing a cab home, both of them jammed in a queue of cars.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stuck in traffic' reads as one phrase, but 'stuck' only lends its final letter and the definition is 'traffic' alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A tailback is a long queue of stationary traffic, as behind roadworks.
annotation.definitionNote: 'traffic' stands for the queue it forms, a tailback

entries.clue: Island nation possessing major airline (6)

indicators.note: the nation holds the airline inside it

annotation.surface: A small island country that happens to own a big airline.
annotation.walkthrough: British Airways is the UK's flag carrier, and the major airline is the thing held inside the West African nation.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain category: the smaller partner in the two-island Caribbean state with Trinidad.

entries.clue: One million reportedly importuned government advance (7)

indicators.note: as it is reported, i.e. spoken: go by the sound

blocks.note: to importune is to press someone; PREST is said like 'pressed'

annotation.surface: A report that someone was pestered a million times for a state loan.
annotation.walkthrough: IMPREST is an obscure word: money advanced from public funds for official spending. The sound trick applies only to 'importuned'.
annotation.definitionFit: An imprest is a sum of money advanced by a government or other body for a particular purpose.

entries.clue: In which Auntie delivers the news? (3,7)

annotation.definition: In which Auntie delivers the news?

blocks.note: reads as a relative; Auntie (Auntie Beeb) is the British nickname for the BBC
reads as passing on gossip; the setter means the accent in which BBC newsreaders read the bulletins

annotation.surface: A family aunt passing on the gossip in her own way.
annotation.walkthrough: Auntie is the BBC, Britain's public broadcaster, and BBC English is the standard accent its newsreaders were once known for.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by function: the standard received pronunciation long associated with the broadcaster's newsreaders.

entries.clue: It’ll make a tidy pile? (6-7)

blocks.note: reads as a machine that stacks things neatly; the setter means one that cleans
reads as a heap; the setter means the soft raised nap of a carpet

annotation.surface: Something that stacks things up neatly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A tidy pile' suggests a neat heap; the pile here is the soft nap of a carpet, which the sweeper leaves clean.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by function: a push-along brush device leaves a carpet's nap clean and tidy.

entries.clue: Shun Dutch artist, losing resistance to whiskey (6)

indicators.note: the artist drops a letter

blocks.note: M. C. Escher, the Dutch graphic artist
R is the symbol for electrical resistance; it is removed

annotation.surface: A painter from Holland giving up his fight against the bottle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To whiskey' in the surface reads as surrender to drink; in the wordplay the R goes and W is added on.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean to avoid deliberately, the answer being the more formal word.

entries.clue: In a nutshell, Louis XIV lost (4)

indicators.note: put briefly, so the name is cut short

blocks.note: Louis XIV of France was known by his nickname as the monarch of the sun; the final three letters are cut

annotation.surface: A summary of how the French king was defeated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a nutshell' reads as 'to sum up', but it is the instruction to shorten the Sun King to its first four letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiomatic synonym: in 'if we miss this train, we're done for', either word fits.

entries.clue: She’ll come into property via hotel, Ireland’s No 1 for staycations (7)

indicators.note: the number-one letter, the first

blocks.note: Eire is Ireland; with the possessive, EIRE'S

annotation.surface: Holiday-at-home promotion for Irish hotels.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a tourism slogan; the definition is a woman who will inherit an estate, and 'property' has nothing to do with hotels.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a woman who will inherit an estate comes into property.

entries.clue: Sadly, wife over end of marriage completely (8)

indicators.note: the end of a word is its closing letter, so only that letter of 'marriage' is used

annotation.surface: A wife, sadly, completely finished with her marriage.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a divorce story; each word supplies a small piece in turn.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both describe doing something in a sorrowful or lamentable way.

entries.clue: Roll article probing oil giant (3)

indicators.note: the article goes into the oil company

annotation.surface: A news article investigating a large oil company.
annotation.walkthrough: A bap is a soft bread roll in Britain; 'Roll' looks like a verb here but is the bread.
annotation.definitionFit: Regional synonym: a British word for a soft round bread roll.

entries.clue: Terrible rains, vacate trailer park (7,4)

indicators.note: the letters are in a terrible state, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: Heavy rain forces holidaymakers to leave a mobile-home park.
annotation.walkthrough: A caravan is the British word for a camper trailer, so the definition is a straight translation.
annotation.definitionFit: Regional synonym: British English calls a trailer a caravan, so the park is the site.

entries.clue: Very poor arcane clue about depleted uranium — it sucks (6,7)

indicators.note: the clue words are in poor order, so rearrange them
the rearranged letters go around the next piece
uranium is emptied, leaving its outside letters

blocks.note: URANIUM depleted to its outer letters, placed inside

annotation.surface: A solver's verdict on an obscure clue: it is really bad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It sucks' reads as slang for 'it's awful', matching the grumble about a poor clue, but it literally describes what the machine does.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the machine cleans by suction, while 'it sucks' also reads as slang for 'it is awful'.

entries.clue: One shelled out 100 Euros up front for pressure group (10)

indicators.note: the first piece goes before the others

blocks.note: a green pea is one taken out of its pod

annotation.surface: Someone paying a hundred euros in advance to a campaign group.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shelled out' looks like 'paid', matching the money; it really means removed from a shell, as peas are.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the environmental campaign organisation is a well-known pressure group.

entries.clue: Staff uniform: list of options (4)

annotation.surface: A dress-code item on a staff noticeboard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' reads as clothing; it is the NATO code word for U.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: on a computer or in a restaurant, a list of options to choose from.

entries.clue: Rolling over in the sack, when topless, such very lewd behaviour (10)

indicators.note: something rolling over turns upside down, so the letters of the phrase are read in reverse
each word loses its top, i.e. first letter

blocks.note: the sack = bed; abed = in bed

annotation.surface: A tabloid-style account of bedroom antics with the clothes off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Topless' fits the racy surface, but it tells you to behead 'such' and 'very'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: excessive indulgence in sensual pleasures.

entries.clue: One enabling record broadcast? (6)

blocks.note: reads as a person who makes something possible; the setter means a small part of a machine
reads as putting a recording on air; the setter means a vinyl record sending out its sound as it plays

annotation.surface: Someone who makes it possible to put a recording on air.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests radio; a stylus is the needle that lets a record be heard.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the needle of a record player reads the groove so the record can be heard.

entries.clue: Universal, endlessly expandable tool (7)

indicators.note: a word without its end is missing its closing letter, so the final E goes

blocks.note: tensile = capable of being stretched; the final E goes

annotation.surface: An advert for a stretchy multi-purpose gadget.
annotation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all ages.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an implement, especially one for the kitchen.

entries.clue: Bind by duty, albeit go easily (8)

indicators.note: the letters go easily, loosely, into a new order

annotation.surface: Advice to hold someone to their obligations, but gently.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go easily' reads as 'take it gently'; 'go' is fodder and 'easily' the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to hold someone to something legally or morally.

entries.clue: Golf club restaurant overlooking East River (7)

indicators.note: ignoring, so leave the letters out

annotation.surface: A golf clubhouse dining room with a view over the East River.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking' sounds like a river view; here it means ignoring. A brassie is an old name for a two-wood.
annotation.definitionFit: Specialist term: an old name for a wooden golf club roughly equal to a two-wood, once soled with brass.

entries.clue: Frail mentally, concealing indisposition (7)

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them

annotation.surface: Someone mentally fragile who is hiding their illness.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is medical, which fits the answer and makes the hidden word easy to overlook.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a mild illness.

entries.clue: Modest Charles Lawrence? (6)

blocks.note: Chas is a short form of Charles
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

annotation.surface: A question about whether a man named Charles Lawrence is modest.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a person's name; it is two people, Chas and T. E. Lawrence.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: pure and modest in conduct.

entries.clue: Gifted group produced megahit (3,4)

indicators.note: the letters are worked up into something new

annotation.surface: A talented band scoring a huge hit record.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gifted' reads as talented; the Magi were gift-givers who brought gold, frankincense and myrrh.
annotation.definitionFit: Allusion: the three wise men brought gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh to the infant Jesus.

entries.clue: “Look up to Cockneys” said prophet (6)

indicators.note: Cockneys drop the H at the start of a word
as spoken, go by the sound

blocks.note: look = 'I say!'; up = HIGH, which a Cockney says as 'IGH

annotation.surface: A prophet telling people to respect Londoners.
annotation.walkthrough: Cockneys are working-class East Londoners, famous for dropping the H. 'I say!' is an old British exclamation, like 'look!'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: an Old Testament prophet with a book of the Bible in his name.

entries.clue: Python moved sideways after shedding skin (4)

indicators.note: the word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: sidled = moved sideways; S and D go

annotation.surface: A snake slithering off sideways after sloughing its skin.
annotation.walkthrough: The snake is a red herring: Python is Monty Python, and Eric Idle was one of the team.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Eric, one of the Monty Python comedy team.

entries.clue: In which there’s a rush to mate? (5,5)

annotation.definition: In which there’s a rush to mate?

blocks.note: reads as a scramble or hurry; the setter means a game played against a very short clock
reads as finding a partner; the setter means delivering checkmate

annotation.surface: A situation where people hurry to find a partner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rush to mate' suggests romance; the mate is checkmate, delivered against the clock.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a form of chess with tight time limits, so every checkmate is hurried.

entries.clue: Cause disturbance in prison (4)

blocks.note: to agitate, as when causing trouble among people

annotation.surface: An inmate making trouble behind bars.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as 'inside', but is only a link between the two meanings.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: to agitate or cause trouble, and old slang for jail.

entries.clue: Gangrene to spread following introduction of awful defoliant (5,6)

indicators.note: the letters spread out into a new order
the rearranged letters come after the first piece
the introduction of a word is its opening, so only its first letter is used

annotation.surface: A medical warning that rot will spread after an awful chemical is introduced.
annotation.walkthrough: Agent Orange was the herbicide sprayed in the Vietnam War; the gruesome surface fits its notoriety.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the herbicide the US military sprayed on Vietnamese jungle to strip the leaves.

entries.clue: Heavyweight tabloid regularly suffering losses (3)

indicators.note: letters are lost at regular intervals, every other one

annotation.surface: A popular newspaper whose circulation keeps falling.
annotation.walkthrough: Muhammad Ali was world heavyweight boxing champion; 'heavyweight' looks like a description of a serious paper, the opposite of a tabloid.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Muhammad, world heavyweight boxing champion.

entries.clue: Restaurant tidier after cancelling New Year (6)

indicators.note: cancelling something removes it, so the N is taken out of the tidier word

annotation.surface: A restaurant looking cleaner after its New Year party was called off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New Year' reads as one holiday; N is taken out and Y is added on.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a casual word for a place to eat.

entries.clue: Caught symptom of plague eating starters of yesterday’s frozen iffy seafood (8)

indicators.note: the rash takes the letters inside it
a starter is what comes first, so each word gives its first letter

annotation.surface: Someone who fell ill from eating yesterday's dodgy frozen seafood.
annotation.walkthrough: The food-poisoning surface fits the answer; 'caught' reads as catching the illness but is the cricket abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: freshwater crustaceans eaten as shellfish.
